name: M15 large-return continuation and reversal screening batch

source_references.citation: Zawadowski, Andor and Kertesz (2006), Short-term market reaction after extreme price changes of liquid stocks, Quantitative Finance 6(4), 283-295
source_references.supports: Causal extreme-move detection and short-horizon reversal as a hypothesis; individual-stock evidence and spread sensitivity do not establish a modern CFD edge.

source_references.citation: Caporale and Plastun (2020), Daily abnormal price changes and trading strategies in the FOREX, Journal of Economic Studies 48(1), 211-222
source_references.supports: Continuation within abnormal FX days and later reversal motivate testing both signs; the published exercise omits executable costs and is not direct M15 evidence.

research.evidence_summary: Adjacent primary studies disagree on continuation versus reversal and do not establish net M15 CFD profitability. This speculative batch tests both signs and retains the adverse prior from I-61 and R-2026-004.

feasibility.rationale: Only causal M1 OHLC, signal-close entry, fixed ATR stops and same-day exits are needed, but V2 compatibility still requires review.

market.session: Signals from completed M15 bars ending 09:00 through 12:45 Europe/London; every exit due no later than 15:00

data.frequency: Complete M1 OHLC bars causally aggregated into half-open M15 intervals
data.minimum_history: Fixed V2 development data only, with 98 valid observed completed M15 closes through the signal bar; elapsed market gaps do not reset prior-only scale or ATR state, but the current signal return requires t-1 and t to be physically adjacent M15 intervals
preprocessing: Treat each stored M1 timestamp as interval start: candle ts covers [ts,ts+1 minute); aggregate exactly 15 consecutive unique valid candles into Europe/London wall-clock quarter-hour buckets, so the M15 bar ending 09:00 contains [08:45,09:00)
Compute M15 log returns, prior-only 96-return MAD scale, and Wilder ATR(20)

Reject non-positive or non-finite OHLC and any bar with high below max(open,close) or low above min(open,close); indicators advance only on valid observed M15 bars, and returns/true ranges across an elapsed gap use the previous observed close so routine daily/weekend gaps remain represented
Convert signal and exit clocks with IANA Europe/London rules
limitations: The family already has adverse exploratory evidence in I-61/R-2026-004
M15 OHLC cannot distinguish information arrival, order flow, bid-ask bounce or temporary liquidity pressure
The six symbols and 48 cells are correlated and are not independent trials
No batch result authorizes final-holdout access

hypothesis.behavior: A completed M15 return unusually large relative to its prior-only robust scale may be followed by short-lived continuation or reversal large enough to survive CFD costs.
hypothesis.mechanism: Continuation may reflect gradual information incorporation or persistent order flow; reversal may reflect temporary liquidity pressure, overreaction or bid-ask effects.
works_when: One response sign persists across neighboring cells and several symbols
The response magnitude exceeds all resolved trading costs
fails_when: The earlier adverse family result generalizes to M15 events
Scheduled news or a few extreme dates create unstable estimates
falsifiable_predictions: A coherent neighboring cluster has positive net R rather than one isolated winning cell
The cluster keeps its sign in both development halves and at least three symbols
The cluster remains positive under doubled costs and after removing the five best dates

definitions.name: observed_return_i
definitions.formula: ln(close_i)-ln(previous_observed_close), including an elapsed market gap
definitions.timing: Advances the prior-only scale only after valid observed M15 bar i closes

definitions.name: event_return_t
definitions.formula: ln(close_t)-ln(close_{t-1}) with t-1 and t required to be physically adjacent 15-minute intervals
definitions.timing: Available only at the close of eligible M15 bar t

definitions.name: robust_scale_t
definitions.formula: 1.4826 * median(abs(observed_return_i-median(observed_return_i))) for the 96 observed returns ending at t-1
definitions.timing: Frozen before event_return_t; require finite and positive

definitions.name: trade_side_t
definitions.formula: sign(event_return_t) for CONTINUATION and its negative for REVERSAL

definitions.name: atr20_t
definitions.formula: Wilder ATR(20) of completed M15 true ranges
definitions.timing: At signal close with no future bar

entries.long_condition: eligible completed M15 bar AND event_score_t >= event_threshold AND ((event_return_t > 0 AND response_mode=CONTINUATION) OR (event_return_t < 0 AND response_mode=REVERSAL)) AND finite positive atr20_t and robust_scale_t AND no open position
entries.short_condition: eligible completed M15 bar AND event_score_t >= event_threshold AND ((event_return_t < 0 AND response_mode=CONTINUATION) OR (event_return_t > 0 AND response_mode=REVERSAL)) AND finite positive atr20_t and robust_scale_t AND no open position
entries.signal_time: Close of a Europe/London-aligned M15 interval ending 09:00 through 12:45 on a weekday when signal time plus holding_minutes is no later than 15:00
entries.execution_details: entry_price is the chart/bid close of M1 [signal_time-1 minute,signal_time), also the completed M15 close. Stop distance is measured from that chart price, not from the cost-adjusted executable fill. V2 separately applies bid/ask-aware spread, commission and slippage to the market fill, using its timestamp-resolved spread or frozen fixed-spread fallback when the feed spread is unavailable. The entry candle's earlier high/low cannot stop the new trade; stop evaluation begins with the next M1 candle. Never substitute next-bar-open.
entries.order_type: Market order at supported signal-close execution
restrictions: One open position per symbol and no pyramiding
Require 98 valid observed M15 closes and require signal bars t-1 and t to be exactly 15 physical minutes apart
Log overlapping events without another entry

exits.stop_loss: Using bid-chart levels, long stop = signal_close_bid-stop_atr_multiplier*atr20_t and short stop = signal_close_bid+stop_atr_multiplier*atr20_t, fixed at entry. V2 triggers long stops from bid and short stops from executable ask (bid plus resolved or fixed-fallback spread), then applies its adverse market-stop fill, commission and slippage; a gap through the executable stop fills at the worse executable opening price.
exits.time_exit: Exit at the close of the completed M1 bar ending exactly signal_time plus holding_minutes; any missing, duplicate, invalid or non-finite M1 interval in (entry_time,due_exit_time] fails the affected cell before a time exit is attempted; if the valid due bar also touches the stop, STOP_LOSS has priority
exits.maximum_holding: At most 120 minutes and never after 15:00 Europe/London
exits.end_of_session: No valid entry may mature after 15:00 Europe/London; no pre-entry bars means no signal, while a post-entry gap before the due exit fails the affected cell

risk.position_sizing: Size so initial entry-to-stop risk equals 0.25% of current equity before costs; never resize
risk.gross_exposure_limit: Maximum six positions and 1.50% aggregate initial stop risk; simultaneous signals use one common pre-entry equity snapshot
risk.leverage: Use the lower of stop-risk size and V2 limits; skip if valid size cannot be represented
risk.concurrent_positions: One per symbol and six across the universe; each symbol is evaluated independently at a shared timestamp

robustness_tests: Report all 48 cells and retain earlier I-61/R-2026-004 trials in multiplicity history

Report every symbol and two halves split at the exact UTC midpoint instant of V2's fixed development [start,end] interval; a bar whose close equals the midpoint belongs to the first half and a later close belongs to the second
Repeat with doubled spread, commission and slippage

For each response mode's center cell k=3/hold=60/stop=1, rank Europe/London dates by pooled net R, break ties by ascending date, remove its top five dates, and apply that same removed-date set to its four declared adjacent cells
Aggregate by Europe/London date and report a 95% percentile interval from 10000 circular five-date block-bootstrap resamples with seed 2026007
A mode advances only if its center cell and at least two of its four exact neighbors (k=2/h=60, k=4/h=60, k=3/h=30, k=3/h=120, all stop=1 and same mode) pass every gate
costs: Use resolved V2 bid/ask-aware spread, commission and slippage at entry, stop and time exit
Doubled-cost stress multiplies spread, commission and slippage individually by two
A gap through a stop fills at V2's worse executable opening price with stop costs and slippage
No swap because all trades exit before 15:00 London
benchmarks: Opposite response mode at identical event and exit settings
Raw direction-normalized forward response before stop-path effects and costs
experiment.multiple_testing: Count all 48 cells plus the 18 frozen R-2026-004 cells and the exact earlier I-61 trials recorded by V2. If the I-61 count cannot be reconstructed, report multiplicity as incomplete and prohibit a confirmatory claim. No best-cell rescue is permitted.
rejection_criteria: Reject a response mode unless its k=3/hold=60/stop=1 center and at least two of the four exact declared neighbors are positive after normal and doubled costs
Reject if the cluster is non-positive in either UTC-midpoint development half
Reject if fewer than three symbols have positive center-cell net R in each fixed development half
Reject if there are fewer than 200 pooled trades
Reject if removing the five best dates makes cluster net R non-positive
Reject on any data-integrity failure that prevents faithful evaluation
Never access the final holdout without explicit authorization for a separately frozen promoted version

pseudocode: Aggregate consecutive completed M1 bars into half-open M15 bars.
Update prior-only 96-return MAD scale and Wilder ATR(20).
At each eligible London-aligned close compute event score and map the declared response sign.
Enter at signal close when flat and freeze the ATR stop and due exit.
Starting with the next M1 candle, process adverse gap stops and intrabar stops before a due time exit using existing V2 fill-cost rules.
Fail an affected cell on any missing, duplicate, invalid or non-finite M1 interval in (entry_time,due_exit_time], including the due interval, before attempting time exit.
Publish every cell and robustness row without selecting a confirmed winner.
required_libraries: existing V2 candle, timezone, cost and R-accounting components
edge_cases: Elapsed pre-entry market gaps remain in observed-sequence return/ATR history but a non-adjacent t-1/t pair cannot signal
DST uses zoneinfo and London wall-clock quarter hours
The entry candle cannot trigger its new stop
A later candle touching stop and due exit resolves stop first; a gap stop uses the worse executable open
Overlapping signals do not reset a trade
In-position data defects fail only the affected cell and must be counted
implementation.computational_requirements: One causal pass per symbol; cache common M15 bars, scales, ATR and events across 48 parameter states.
known_backtester_gaps: SUPPORTED denotes that all six symbols and OHLC fields are in the published V2 capability snapshot; queue submission remains gated on V2 confirming the custom London-aligned M15 state, independent 48-cell execution, failure accounting and required result rows
